title: 근육이 빠지는 근감소증, 걷기만으로 충분할까요
description: 나이 들며 근육과 힘이 함께 줄어드는 근감소증과 걷기의 관계를 어르신 23만여 명 자료와 운동 시험 분석으로 쉽게 풀고, 집에서 곁들일 근력 운동도 소개했어요.

body_markdown:
시장에 다녀오신 어머니가 "장바구니가 예전 같지 않다"고 하시거나, 아버지가 의자에서 일어나실 때 팔걸이를 꼭 짚으시는 모습을 보신 적 있으신가요? 나이 들면 다 그렇다고 넘기기 쉽지만, 근육이 줄어드는 것도 살펴볼 만한 몸의 변화예요. 오늘은 근감소증과 걷기에 관한 연구를 쉽게 풀어 볼게요.

## 근감소증, 근육과 힘이 함께 줄어드는 것

근감소증은 나이가 들며 근육의 양과 힘, 몸을 움직이는 능력이 함께 떨어지는 상태를 말해요. 한 리뷰 논문은 60세가 넘으면 근육량은 해마다 약 1%, 근력은 해마다 약 3%씩 줄어든다는 추정을 소개했어요 [3]. 근육보다 힘이 더 빨리 줄어든다는 뜻이지요. 이런 변화는 낙상과 골절, 입원, 움직임이 불편해지는 일과 관련이 있다고 해요 [3].

이 논문이 강조한 대목이 하나 더 있어요. 근육은 해마다 똑같은 속도로 줄지 않고, 아프셔서 누워 지내시거나 바깥출입이 줄어 하루 걸음 수가 크게 떨어진 시기에 더 빨리 줄어든다는 거예요. 그리고 어르신은 그런 시기를 지나고 나서 회복이 느리거나 다 돌아오지 않을 수 있다고 봤어요 [3]. 감기 몸살로 일주일 집에만 계셨던 뒤에 다리에 힘이 빠졌다고 하시는 것도 이런 흐름과 맞닿아 있어요.

## 23만 명 어르신 자료로 본 움직임과 근감소증

2024년 국제 학술지 랜싯의 노년 건강 분야 학술지에는 신체활동과 근감소증의 관계를 모은 분석이 실렸어요 [1]. 124개 연구, 어르신 230,174명의 자료를 정리했고, 그 가운데 86개 연구를 묶어 계산했어요. 결과를 보면 신체활동이 많은 어르신일수록 근감소증이 있을 가능성이 낮았어요. 한 시점에 함께 잰 연구에서는 오즈비가 0.49였고, 오래 지켜본 연구에서도 0.51이었어요 [1]. 오즈비가 0.49라는 것은 근감소증이 있을 가능성이 대략 절반 정도였다는 뜻으로 읽으면 돼요.

흥미로운 점도 있어요. 숨이 조금 찰 정도의 중간 강도 이상 활동은 근감소증과 관련이 있었지만, 걸음 수나 가벼운 활동, 앉아 있는 시간은 뚜렷한 관련이 나타나지 않았어요 [1]. 그래서 연구진은 가벼운 활동보다 중간 강도 이상의 활동이 중요할 수 있다고 해석했어요.

## 하루 걸음 수를 1년 동안 지켜본 연구

반대로 걸음 수와의 관련을 본 연구도 있어요. 중국에서 1,281명의 하루 걸음 수를 스마트폰으로 재며 1년 동안 지켜본 연구예요 [4]. 걸음 수가 적었던 분들은 1년 뒤 근감소증과 관련이 있었고, 거꾸로 근감소증이 있던 분들은 1년 뒤 걸음 수가 줄어드는 쪽이었어요. 근육이 줄면 덜 걷게 되고, 덜 걸으면 근육이 더 줄어드는 서로 맞물린 관계로 볼 수 있지요. 연구진은 하루 4,888보 언저리를 근감소증이 새로 생길지 가늠하는 기준점으로 제시했어요 [4]. 다만 참여자의 평균 나이가 52.1세로 어르신만의 결과는 아니었어요.

두 연구의 결과가 조금 다르지요? 그만큼 걸음 수 하나로 근육 건강을 다 설명하기는 어렵다는 뜻이에요. 많이 걷는 것과 함께, 조금 힘 있게 걷는 것도 챙겨 볼 만해요.

## 걷기에 근력 운동을 더하면

근감소증이 이미 있는 어르신에게는 어떤 운동이 도움이 되었을까요? 2023년에 나온 분석은 무작위 시험 42개, 근감소증이 있는 3728명을 모아 운동 종류를 서로 비교했어요 [2]. 참여자 나이의 중앙값은 72.9세였고 73.3%가 여성이었어요. 삶의 질을 높이는 데에는 근력 운동, 그리고 근력 운동에 걷기 같은 유산소 운동과 균형 운동을 함께한 방법이 가장 좋아지는 쪽이었어요. 근력 운동과 균형 운동을 함께하면 평소 걸음 속도가 1초에 0.16미터 빨라지는 쪽이었고, 여기에 영양 관리를 더하면 손아귀 힘이 더 좋아지는 쪽이었어요 [2].

걷기만으로 근육을 다 지키기는 어렵고, 걷기에 근력 운동을 곁들일 때 더 나은 결과가 나왔다는 이야기예요. 세계보건기구도 65세 이상 어르신께 유산소 활동과 함께 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상 하시길 권해요 [5].

## 이 연구들로 말할 수 없는 것

신체활동과 걸음 수를 다룬 연구는 관계를 본 관찰연구예요 [1][4]. 많이 움직여서 근육이 덜 줄어든 것인지, 근육이 튼튼한 분이 원래 더 많이 움직이신 것인지는 가릴 수 없어요. 운동 시험들도 대부분 12주 안팎의 짧은 기간이었어요 [2]. 또 근감소증은 근육량과 악력, 걸음 속도를 함께 보고 판단하는 것이라, 집에서 걷는 모습만으로 알 수는 없어요. 걱정되신다면 의료진과 상의해 보세요.

## 부모님과 함께 해 볼 작은 실천

먼저 걷는 날을 꾸준히 이어 가세요. 몸이 아파 며칠 쉬셨다면, 회복되시는 대로 집 안이나 집 앞에서라도 조금씩 걸음을 다시 늘려 가시는 것이 좋아요. 걸을 때는 옆 사람과 이야기는 되지만 조금 숨이 찰 만큼 걸어 보세요. 여기에 집에서 할 수 있는 근력 운동을 곁들여 보세요. 튼튼한 의자에서 천천히 일어났다 앉기, 식탁을 잡고 발뒤꿈치 들기처럼 간단한 동작부터 시작하면 돼요. 무릎이나 허리가 아프시거나 넘어진 적이 있으시다면 무리하지 마시고 의료진과 먼저 상의하세요. 끼니마다 고기, 생선, 달걀, 두부 같은 반찬을 곁들이시는지도 함께 살펴봐 주세요.

근육은 하루아침에 생기지도, 사라지지도 않아요. 그래서 함께 걷는 날이 쌓이는 것이 가장 든든해요. 이번 주말에는 부모님과 시장까지 천천히 걸어가 장을 함께 보고 오시면 어떨까요?

sources.title: Association of physical behaviours with sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Physical behaviours (ie, physical activity and sedentary behaviour) might have a role in the development of sarcopenia, although the evidence is unclear. We aimed to explore the association of total and intensity-specific levels of physical activity and sedentary behaviour with sarcopenia and its components (ie, muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance) in older adults. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis and searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to July 26, 2022, for peer-reviewed, observational studies or baseline data from randomised clinical trials conducted in older adults (ie, individual age ≥60 years or mean age ≥65 years) and published in English that reported on the association of physical activity or sedentary behaviour or both with sarcopenia (or its determinants: muscle mass or strength, and physical performance). Physical activity and sedentary behaviour were measured by any method. The main outcome was sarcopenia, which could be diagnosed by any means. Estimates were extracted and pooled using Bayesian meta-analytic models and publication bias was assessed using the Egger's test. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD42022315865. FINDINGS: We identified 15 766 records, of which 124 studies (230 174 older adults; 121 301 [52·7%] were female and 108 873 [47·3%] were male) were included in the systematic review. 86 studies were subsequently included in the meta-analysis. Higher levels of total physical activity were inversely associated with sarcopenia both cross-sectionally (21 studies, n=59 572; odds ratio 0·49, 95% credible interval 0·37-0·62) and longitudinally (four studies, n=7545; 0·51, 0·27-0·94). A protective association was also identified for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in cross-sectional research (five studies, n=6787; 0·85, 0·71-0·99), whereas no association was identified for the remaining physical behaviours (ie, steps, light physical activity, or sedentary behaviour). INTERPRETATION: Total and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity are inversely associated with sarcopenia. These findings might support the importance of moderate-to-vigorous, rather than light, intensity physical activity-based interventions to prevent sarcopenia. FUNDING: None. TRANSLATION: For the Spanish translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

sources.title: Exercise for sarcopenia in older people: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
sources.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a serious public health concern among older adults worldwide. Exercise is the most common intervention for sarcopenia. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of different exercise types for older adults with sarcopenia. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that examined the effectiveness of exercise interventions on patient-important outcomes for older adults with sarcopenia were eligible. We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials via Ovid until 3 June 2022. We used frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses to summarize the evidence and applied the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations framework to rate the certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Our search identified 5988 citations, of which 42 RCTs proved eligible with 3728 participants with sarcopenia (median age: 72.9 years, female: 73.3%) with a median follow-up of 12 weeks. We are interested in patient-important outcomes that include mortality, quality of life, muscle strength and physical function measures. High or moderate certainty evidence suggested that resistance exercise with or without nutrition and the combination of resistance exercise with aerobic and balance training were the most effective interventions for improving quality of life compared to usual care (standardized mean difference from 0.68 to 1.11). Moderate certainty evidence showed that resistance and balance exercise plus nutrition (mean difference [MD]: 4.19 kg) was the most effective for improving handgrip strength (minimally important difference [MID]: 5 kg). Resistance and balance exercise with or without nutrition (MD: 0.16 m/s, moderate) were the most effective for improving physical function measured by usual gait speed (MID: 0.1 m/s). Moderate certainty evidence showed that resistance and balance exercise (MD: 1.85 s) was intermediately effective for improving physical function measured by timed up and go test (MID: 2.1 s). High certainty evidence showed that resistance and aerobic, or resistance and balance, or resistance and aerobic exercise plus nutrition (MD from 1.72 to 2.28 s) were intermediately effective for improving physical function measured by the five-repetition chair stand test (MID: 2.3 s). CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with sarcopenia, high or moderate certainty evidence showed that resistance exercise with or without nutrition and the combination of resistance exercise with aerobic and balance training were the most effective interventions for improving quality of life. Adding nutritional interventions to exercise had a larger effect on handgrip strength than exercise alone while showing a similar effect on other physical function measures.

sources.title: The Impact of Step Reduction on Muscle Health in Aging: Protein and Exercise as Countermeasures.
sources.text: Declines in strength and muscle function with age-sarcopenia-contribute to a variety of negative outcomes including an increased risk of: falls, fractures, hospitalization, and reduced mobility in older persons. Population-based estimates of the loss of muscle after age 60 show a loss of ~1% per year while strength loss is more rapid at ~3% per year. These rates are not, however, linear as periodic bouts of reduced physical activity and muscle disuse transiently accelerate loss of muscle and declines in muscle strength and power. Episodic complete muscle disuse can be due to sickness-related bed rest or local muscle disuse as a result of limb immobilization/surgery. Alternatively, relative muscle disuse occurs during inactivity due to illness and the associated convalescence resulting in marked reductions in daily steps, often referred to as step reduction (SR). While it is a "milder" form of disuse, it can have a similar adverse impact on skeletal muscle health. The physiological consequences of even short-term inactivity, modeled by SR, show losses in muscle mass and strength, as well as impaired insulin sensitivity and an increase in systemic inflammation. Though seemingly benign in comparison to bed rest, periodic inactivity likely occurs, we posit, more frequently with advancing age due to illness, declining mental health and declining mobility. Given that recovery from inactivity in older adults is slow or possibly incomplete we hypothesize that accumulated periods of inactivity contribute to sarcopenia. Periodic activity, even in small quantities, and protein supplementation may serve as effective strategies to offset the loss of muscle mass with aging, specifically during periods of inactivity. The aim of this review is to examine the recent literature encompassing SR, as a model of inactivity, and to explore the capacity of nutrition and exercise interventions to mitigate adverse physiological changes as a result of SR.

sources.title: Bidirectional association of daily steps with sarcopenia: a longitudinal study.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Step count is a well-established measure of physical activity, and step-based recommendations offering practical public guidance. However, the bidirectional associations between step count and sarcopenia remain unclear, limiting the application of step-based interventions for sarcopenia prevention. This study examined the directional association between daily steps and sarcopenia. METHODS: Data were collected from the Xiangya Step Study (a population-based longitudinal study) between January 2020 and December 2022. Average daily steps were tracked via smartphones linked to WeChat, a social networking platform. Sarcopenia was diagnosed using the Asian Workgroup of Sarcopenia 2019 criteria. A two-wave cross-lagged panel model was used to evaluate bidirectional associations between daily steps and sarcopenia. Additionally, logistic regression examines the association between daily steps and incident sarcopenia risk in participants without sarcopenia at baseline. The area under the curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the predictive performance of baseline daily steps for incident sarcopenia. RESULTS: The study included 1,281 participants (30.1% women), averaging 52.1 years. A significant bidirectional association was observed: fewer daily steps at baseline were associated with sarcopenia status one year later (cross-lagged path coefficient [β]=-1.20, 95%CI: -1.90 to -0.50, p = 0.001), and sarcopenia status at baseline was associated with decreased daily steps one year later (β=-0.19, 95%CI: -0.23 to -0.15, p < 0.001). Logistic regression indicated that each standard deviation increase in daily steps was associated with a lower risk of incident sarcopenia (adjusted OR = 0.28, 95%CI: 0.09 to 0.89, p = 0.03). The AUC for daily steps was 0.74 (95%CI: 0.56 to 0.92), with an optimal cutoff of 4,888 steps (sensitivity = 0.62, specificity = 0.85). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights a bidirectional inverse association between average daily steps and sarcopenia. Increasing daily steps, especially to 5,000, might help mitigate sarcopenia development. Future research could explore interventions that increase daily steps to prevent sarcopenia and investigate whether sarcopenia reversal could improve physical activity levels. In this longitudinal cohort study involving 1,281 middle-aged and elderly adults, we identified a bidirectional and inverse association between daily steps and sarcopenia.The receiver operating characteristic curve suggested that a threshold of 4,888 steps had moderate predictive power for incident sarcopenia.Our findings suggest that increasing daily step counts, particularly achieving a public-acceptable threshold of 5,000 steps, has the potential to mitigate the development of sarcopenia.

sources.text: 65세 이상 어르신 권고: 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 신체활동 150~300분 이상, 또는 고강도 75~150분 이상. 중간 강도 이상의 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상. 기능적 균형과 근력을 강조한 복합 신체활동을 일주일에 3일 이상(기능을 높이고 낙상을 막기 위해). 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이고 어떤 강도든 신체활동으로 바꾸는 것이 건강에 이롭다. 권고량을 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다.
